compat_drain_window.policy: legacy workflow remains available only for replay-safe compatibility and explicit controlled drain
compat_drain_window.open_condition: legacy workflow histories still exist or explicit replay/drain signoff is not yet captured for the target environment
close_condition: legacy replay evidence proves total_runs=0 and open_runs=0 for the target environment, or a production replay/drain signoff artifact proves all remaining histories drained safely
forward workflow is the default operator path for new site-build and rebuild execution
production gate targets the forward workflow rather than the legacy workflow
legacy workflow remains excluded from new feature work
compat_drain_window.current_verdict: closed for the current local environment because the recorded legacy replay evidence shows no historical SeoSiteBuildWorkflow executions

expert_workflow_policy.retirement_decision: keep as narrow diagnostic toolset during compat/drain; delete later only if they stop providing unique replay/migration debugging value

workflow_naming_decision.decision: keep SeoSiteBuildCanonicalCutoverWorkflow as the runtime workflow type after drain; do not create a new workflow type purely to rename it
workflow_naming_decision.operator_policy: docs and starter should treat this workflow as the canonical forward path; legacy SeoSiteBuildWorkflow stays compat-only
workflow_naming_decision.future_rename_rule: a future rename is allowed only if another workflow-semantics change already requires a new workflow type, or if a dedicated zero-history cleanup window is explicitly approved
rationale: renaming only for cosmetics creates another migration surface without increasing correctness
the current workflow type already has accepted end-to-end evidence and production-gate alignment
operator confusion is better solved through docs, starter defaults, and legacy quarantine than by introducing another runtime identity
